title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a cover sheet or plan for a section. It has a crossed-out title, 'Déformations des groupes de B.T. ordinaires', replaced by two headings.

(1) 'Détermination des "stratifications canoniques" sur les déformations.' The next page makes the meaning precise. Take an abelian variety A_0 over a field k of characteristic p. The question is when one can attach, functorially in A and compatibly with base change, a k-stratification (a crystal or HPD-stratification structure, i.e. a canonical integrable connection) on DR^1(A/Λ) for every infinitesimal deformation A/Λ over Artinian local k-algebras.
- Necessary condition: on the formal moduli M with universal deformation A_M, the module H = DR^1(A_M/M) must carry a formal stratification compatible with F and V.
- Consequence: the geometric type of (H_x, F_x, V_x) is constant on M.
- This forces A_0 to be ordinary: Ker F = Im V, and the p-linear map on H^1(A_0, O) is bijective.
- In the ordinary case, Im F maps isomorphically onto H^{01}. This splits the Hodge extension 0→H^{10}→H→H^{01}→0 canonically. This is the Dwork/Katz unit-root splitting, the char-p shadow of Serre–Tate canonical coordinates.
- The original title shows the intended object: deformations of ordinary Barsotti–Tate groups. Their deformation space is the formal torus Hom(T_p(A_0)_et ⊗ T_p(A_0^*)_et, Ĝ_m) (Serre–Tate).

(2) 'L'isom. de nature globale: det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A^*)_et.' Over an ordinary base, T_p(A)_et and T_p(A^*)_et are lisse Z_p-sheaves of rank g. The boxed claim is that their determinants are canonically isomorphic as rank-one local systems.
- It is 'global' because infinitesimally, on deformation spaces with algebraically closed residue field, étale sheaves are constant, so deformation theory sees nothing.
- Natural proof in crystalline terms. The unit-root part of H^1_cris(A) corresponds to one étale Tate module. The slope-1 part corresponds to the dual of the other, via Cartier duality between A[p^∞]^mult and A^*[p^∞]^et.
- Then det H^1_cris(A) = Λ^{2g}H^1 = H^{2g}_cris(A), which is ≅ O(−g) canonically by the trace map. Hence the two unit-root determinant characters agree.
- The de Rham shadow is the known canonical isomorphism det ω_A ≅ det ω_{A^*}, from det H^1_dR ≅ O.
- Alternatively: any polarization or isogeny f gives det T_p(f)_et, which is injective with image p^k·det. Dividing by p^k gives an isomorphism, but naturality then needs checking.

The connection to the previous page (inertia action and constancy of pA) is thematic only: étale parts of Tate modules and their determinants.
errors: No explicit errors; the page only states headings. The boxed isomorphism is correct, e.g. via the trace on H^{2g}_cris = Λ^{2g}H^1. Its canonicity, i.e. independence of auxiliary choices such as a polarization, is not addressed on the page.

ideas.what: Canonical stratification (connection) on DR^1 of deformations, existing essentially only for ordinary A_0
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical coordinates / Dwork–Katz unit-root splitting of the Hodge filtration on the ordinary locus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (1964), Dwork, Katz ('Serre–Tate local moduli', 1981), Messing (1972)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970/74); unsure

ideas.what: Global isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A^*)_et of rank-one étale Z_p-local systems on the ordinary locus
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of unit-root F-crystals; consequence of H^{2g}_cris(A) ≅ O(−g) and Cartier duality; de Rham shadow det ω_A ≅ det ω_{A^t}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; det ω_A ≅ det ω_{A^t} appears in Moret-Bailly and Faltings–Chai type treatments

missed.claim: A planned characterization: functorial canonical stratifications on DR^1 of infinitesimal deformations exist iff A_0 is ordinary. This is stated on the next page as 'sans doute'. The planned treatment of 'déformations des groupes de B.T. ordinaires' was abandoned (title crossed out).
missed.quote: Determination des "stratifications canoniques" sur les déformations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly subsumed by Serre–Tate/Katz theory. An explicit 'iff' characterization in terms of functorial stratifications is a minor point, not prominently stated in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a planning page. Both ideas, canonical structure on ordinary deformations and the determinant isomorphism of étale Tate modules, are standard or folklore today: Serre–Tate, Katz, and the trace on H^{2g}. Their only interest is showing Grothendieck working on these questions around 1969.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially correct. 'sur les déformations' is written over a struck word, likely 'les'. The subscript in the box is 'et' (étale) on both sides, and A* is the dual abelian variety.
